data.name: Dhruvabhak
data.gender_notes: Dhruvabhak is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Dhruvabhak represents the unwavering star, symbolizing unflinching devotion. The name Dhruvabhak carries the meaning “Star of the Heart” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dhruvabhak usually hope their child will grow to embody star of the heart and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A beacon of light and devotion, inspiring unwavering faith and commitment.
data.etymology: Dhruvabhak belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Star of the Heart.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dhruvabhak total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dhruvabhak holds a deep cultural significance in Indian mythology. It is derived from the story of King Dhruva, who was known for his unwavering devotion to Lord Mahavishnu. King Dhruva's unwavering commitment to the deity earned him a place in the stars as the Pole Star, known as Dhruva Tara. The name reflects the value of unwavering faith, loyalty, and devotion to a higher power in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Besides its cultural significance, the name Dhruvabhak holds a profound spiritual meaning. It represents the human spirit's unwavering search for truth and the divine. The name signifies the inner strength and resilience required to remain committed to our spiritual goals, no matter the challenges we face. It is a reminder that, like the star Dhruva, we too can navigate through life's complexities with unwavering dedication to our spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dhruva signifies unwavering determination and devotion towards a goal. Bhak means devotion. Thus, Dhruvabhak symbolizes an individual with unwavering devotion towards a divine goal or path.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas, Upanishads, or other scriptures

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, King Dhruva was a virtuous ruler who, due to his unwavering devotion to Lord Vishnu, was granted a boon to regain his lost kingdom. The story is described in detail in various Hindu texts, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

Another reference to Dhruvabhak can be found in the 13th-century Sanskrit epic, the Jaina Bhagavati. In this text, Dhruvabhak is mentioned as a Jaina monk who attained spiritual enlightenment under the guidance of Mahavira.
